answer:
Verdict: no

## What the trace shows

Over the whole trace (0–30,608.7 ms), jobrunner (PID 658444) exited normally with status 0 at 30,095.8 ms—about 512.8 ms before the trace ended. The trace therefore shows no jobrunner threads still alive at its end.

Before exit, TID 658444 (jobrunner) spent most of its time waiting, mainly on a timer. The watchdog and TIDs 658446–658449 (`job-0` through `job-3`) were blocked for about 30 seconds and were woken by the main thread. The lifecycle finding says the threads doing most of the work last ran at 30,017.7 ms, followed by a fast 78.1 ms shutdown.

The trace shows when work threads last ran and when the process exited, but it does not establish whether the program’s intended work was semantically complete.
